name: sms_hitl_flow: outbound SMS sent on HITL request; stored in vault
notes: When a HITL decision is requested the adapter MUST:
(a) send an outbound SMS to the operator phone via AWS End User Messaging
(PinpointSMSVoiceV2 SendTextMessage),
(b) store the outbound message ID and body in the tenant vault under
a receipt-scoped key so the audit trail is complete.
Transport pivot: Twilio -> AWS End User Messaging (S2.1 Sprint 2).
Outbound message IDs are AWS-assigned UUIDs (not SM-prefixed Twilio SIDs).
Sandbox note: without 10DLC registration AWS delivers only to VERIFIED
destination numbers registered in the AWS console. Joshua and Steve must
be added as verified destinations before the demo.
Falsifiability: remove the vault.put call after the AWS outbound send.
The FeedResult.stored_in_vault field will be absent or false and this
vector fails at the expected_outbound_shape assertion.
Spec reference: S2.1 SMS-HITL adapter, vault storage contract.

name: sms_hitl_flow: inbound YES via SNS notification triggers D1 -> E1 replay chain
notes: An AWS SNS Notification arriving at POST /v1/agp/hitl/sns/inbound with
messageBody='YES' must:
(a) validate the TopicArn against AWS_SNS_INBOUND_TOPIC_ARN env var,
(b) resolve the pending HITL request (identified by originationNumber
matching the outbound phone record),
(c) emit a D1 denial receipt (status=denied, detail='HITL pending'),
(d) then immediately emit an E1 execution receipt (status=ok, replayed_after=D1.oid).
Signal OID uses 'aws-sms:<inboundMessageId>' prefix (was 'twilio:' before pivot).
Falsifiability: strip the replayed_after field from E1 body. The assertion
e1_replayed_after_equals_d1_oid fails with field-absent error.
Spec reference: S2.3 replay-chain contract; S2.1 HITL inbound handler.

assertions.note: TopicArn must match AWS_SNS_INBOUND_TOPIC_ARN before any action is taken
D1 is always a denial receipt marking the HITL pending state
denial detail must describe the HITL pending state
E1 is the execution receipt after HITL approval
E1.body.replayed_after must equal D1.oid to anchor the replay chain
E1.prev (Merkle parent) must also equal D1.oid

name: sms_hitl_flow: inbound NO via SNS notification emits denial receipt with reason=hitl_denied
notes: An SNS Notification with messageBody='NO' (case-insensitive) must:
emit a denial receipt with decision=deny and detail containing 'hitl_denied'.
No E1 execution receipt is emitted. The provisional block remains.
Falsifiability: change the gate to emit an allow receipt on 'NO' body.
The assertion denial_receipt_emitted fails.
Spec reference: S2.1 HITL inbound handler; GAP denial receipt contract.

assertions.note: TopicArn verified even on NO path
A denial receipt must be emitted on NO
detail must contain 'hitl_denied' so the verifier can distinguish from other denial reasons
No E1 execution receipt on NO

name: sms_hitl_flow: unknown SNS topic ARN on inbound is rejected
notes: An SNS Notification POST with a TopicArn that does not match
AWS_SNS_INBOUND_TOPIC_ARN must be rejected immediately with HTTP 403.
No receipt is emitted; no vault writes occur for the spoofed inbound.
Bypass via SYNOI_SMS_SKIP_SIG=1 for dev/test.
Falsifiability: skip the topic ARN check. The gate accepts notifications
from arbitrary SNS topics and emits receipts for unauthenticated events.
The assertion error_kind=unknown_sns_topic fails.
Spec reference: S2.1 SNS topic validation contract.

assertions.note: Gate must return unknown_sns_topic for unrecognized TopicArn
No receipt is emitted for an unrecognized topic

name: sms_hitl_flow: expired window (>5 min after D1) auto-lifts and rejects late inbound
expected_error_detail: HITL reply window expired (>5 min since D1); inbound rejected
notes: The HITL reply window is 5 minutes from the D1 creation timestamp.
After that window the gate auto-lifts: the provisional block is cleared and
any inbound reply (even a valid YES) is rejected as hitl_window_expired.
The auto-lift itself emits a denial receipt with decision=deny, detail='hitl_timeout'.
Falsifiability: remove the window check. A late YES reply is processed as if
the window were still open and the gate emits an E1 -- this vector fails.
Spec reference: S2.1 HITL timeout/auto-lift contract.
Note: the 5-minute window here (C6) is distinct from the 72-hour provisional
block window in the replay-chain gate (C9). The HITL window guards SMS reply
liveness; the replay-chain window guards chain anchor freshness.

assertions.note: Gate must return hitl_window_expired after 5-minute window
Auto-lift must emit a denial receipt with detail=hitl_timeout
auto-lift denial receipt detail must contain 'hitl_timeout'

name: sms_hitl_flow: SNS SubscriptionConfirmation auto-confirmed
notes: When AWS SNS sends a SubscriptionConfirmation message to
POST /v1/agp/hitl/sns/inbound, the endpoint MUST respond 200 and
auto-confirm by GET-ing the SubscribeURL supplied in the envelope.
The SubscribeURL is issued and signed by AWS; the gateway only GETs it.
Falsifiability: skip the SubscribeURL GET. The subscription remains
unconfirmed and AWS never delivers Notification messages.
Spec reference: AWS SNS subscription confirmation protocol.

assertions.note: Endpoint must return 200 to acknowledge the confirmation request
SubscribeURL must be GET-ed to confirm the subscription

name: sms_hitl_flow: SIM-swap residual disclosure annotation (render_contract; not pass/fail gate)
notes: C6 / S2.9 / ARCH.1 Section 17.
SIM-swap is a known residual risk for SMS-based HITL: a carrier-level SIM transfer
could allow a different device to receive the SMS. This applies regardless of
whether the transport is Twilio or AWS End User Messaging -- both are telephony
channels, not cryptographic ones. This is NOT a bug in the gate;
it is an acknowledged limitation of SMS as the HITL channel.
The verifier UI MUST render an honest disclosure when subject_type=sms_hitl:
'SMS HITL approval is subject to SIM-swap risk. WebAuthn push approval eliminates
this residual. See Section 17 of the conformance spec.'
Roadmap fix: WebAuthn push notification replaces SMS as the HITL channel for
high-assurance operators. Until then, the disclosure is mandatory in the verifier.
This vector is annotation_only: it does not produce a pass or fail on the HITL
implementation itself, only on the verifier UI rendering of the receipt.

render_contract.roadmap_note: WebAuthn push approval eliminates SIM-swap residual (not yet shipped as of 2026-06-18)
notes: The disclosure must be honest: SMS is a telephony channel, not a cryptographic one.
Forbidden labels would overclaim the channel's security properties.
Until WebAuthn ships, the verifier must not label SMS-HITL as an independent signal.
This applies to both Twilio and AWS End User Messaging transports.
